Evidence: Kerala has imposed stricter Covid-19 curbs as four districts—Idukki, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, and Kollam—have been added to the existing 'C' category, which indicates rapidly rising cases. Thiruvananthapuram remains in this category as well. In 'C' category districts, public functions are banned, and only online religious events are allowed. Gyms, swimming pools, and theaters are closed. Classes for grades one to nine are conducted online, while physical attendance is permitted only for final year students. This information is corroborated by Source 1 and Source 2.
Justification: The retrieved evidence directly states that Kerala has implemented more strict curbs due to the inclusion of four districts in the 'C' category, which signifies a rise in Covid-19 cases. Source 1 confirms the addition of these districts and outlines the restrictions imposed, such as banning public functions and closing gyms and theaters. Source 2 further explains the implications of being in the 'C' category, supporting the claim that stricter measures are in place in Kerala.
